cf.title: Report unsupported COPY FROM targets before reading input

input.subject: Reject unsupported COPY FROM targets before analyzing WHERE clause

verdict_reasoning: No objection survived the critic. The only one raised, maintenance-fit-1, was refuted because the moved relkind check accepts foreign tables and file_fdw passes with v3. The change moves an existing check to the place COPY TO already uses, and its cost falls only on commands that fail anyway. Confidence is medium because the code was not read and no committer has replied.

brief.title: Report unsupported COPY FROM targets before reading input
brief.problem: COPY FROM a sequence, view or other unsupported target only fails with "cannot copy to sequence" after psql has entered COPY input mode and the user has typed data. On master the server also opens the input file or runs the PROGRAM command before it rejects the target. The author frames this as poor user experience, not a correctness bug.
brief.proposed_design: v3 moves the relation-kind check from CopyFrom() to BeginCopyFrom(), so it runs before the server reads input, opens a file or starts a program. Parse analysis, permission, column-list and WHERE-clause errors still come first, matching COPY TO, which checks relkind in BeginCopyTo(). v1 also put the check before WHERE-clause analysis, but the author dropped that after review.
user_visible_surface: COPY FROM an unsupported target (sequence, view, matview) fails before entering COPY input mode.
COPY FROM PROGRAM on an unsupported target no longer runs the program before the error.
COPY seq FROM '/nonexistent/file' now reports "cannot copy to sequence" instead of "could not open file".
Invalid COPY options such as (format bogus) are now reported after the relkind error.
file_fdw gets the earlier check through BeginCopyFrom(), per a reviewer.
author_claims: Failing before waiting for input is a better user experience.
The change keeps the existing order of parse, permission and WHERE-clause errors.
The change makes COPY FROM consistent with COPY TO.
The change avoids opening the input file or starting an external program for a command that will fail.
brief.thread_state: Horiguchi pushed back on reordering against WHERE-clause errors, and the author narrowed the patch in v2. Liu, solai v and Poondla tested v2/v3 and gave +1; no committer has replied, and the author plans to revisit check ordering for v20.
unclear: The patch adds no test for the early failure; a reviewer suggested one with a nonexistent file.
The commit message does not mention that option errors now come after the relkind error.
The material does not say whether any other BeginCopyFrom() caller depends on the old check placement.
The CommitFest entry targets version 19, but the thread tests on 20devel.
search_queries: COPY FROM STDIN error before input

refuted.title: Write-target check moves into BeginCopyFrom(), which read-only callers also use
refuted.failure_scenario: A third-party FDW calls BeginCopyFrom() with its own foreign table only to parse a file, and never calls CopyFrom(). After this change that FDW may start failing with "cannot copy to foreign table". The FDW author finds out after upgrading Postgres.
refuted.argument: BeginCopyFrom() is exported, and file_fdw uses it to read, not to insert, as message #4 notes. The relkind check answers whether the relation can take inserts, which only CopyFrom() needs. The proposal does not say how the moved check treats callers that never insert, or why file_fdw is unaffected. Message #8 reports that file_fdw tests pass, but the commit message names no rule for out-of-tree callers.
refuted.author_must_show: Does the moved check in BeginCopyFrom() run for callers that never call CopyFrom(), and if not, what rule decides that for extensions?

critic.reasoning: The relkind check in CopyFrom() accepts foreign tables and rejects only views, matviews, sequences and other non-table relations. An FDW that passes its own foreign table to BeginCopyFrom() does not hit it, and message #8 reports that file_fdw passes with v3.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: BeginCopyFrom() is exported and used by file_fdw; it now rejects unsupported relation kinds itself.

touch_points.label: psql UX conventions
touch_points.reason: psql no longer enters COPY input mode for COPY FROM STDIN on a sequence, view or matview.

touch_points.label: security / privileges
touch_points.reason: COPY FROM PROGRAM on an unsupported target no longer runs the program; permission checks still come first.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Will the patch add a regression test for the early failure, such as COPY of a sequence FROM a nonexistent file, as a reviewer suggested?
Should the commit message say that invalid COPY options such as (format bogus) are now reported after the relkind error?
Can an out-of-tree caller of BeginCopyFrom() pass a relation kind that the moved check rejects but that worked before because the caller never called CopyFrom()?
Which release does the patch target, given that the CommitFest entry says 19 and the thread tests on 20devel?

committability.owner_note: A committer who knows the COPY code in src/backend/commands and the BeginCopyFrom() callers (file_fdw, tablesync) would have to own it. None has replied in the visible thread.
committability.liability: The owner signs for a changed error order in COPY FROM commands that fail and for BeginCopyFrom() now rejecting unsupported relation kinds for all callers. The exposure is small and limited to one file.
committability.author_follow_up: The author revised the patch after review (v1 to v3) and says in message #3 that he plans further work on check ordering for v20.

priority.reason: The v3 patch is 4.8 KB in copyfrom.c, adds no user-visible surface and helps only users who run COPY FROM on an unsupported target. Three reviewers gave +1 over three CommitFests, but no committer has replied.

provisional_note: The code was not read, so the exact position of the moved check among the other BeginCopyFrom() steps is unverified. Its effect on out-of-tree BeginCopyFrom() callers rests on the critic's reading and the reported file_fdw test result.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch fixes an out-of-bounds read in COPY FROM with on_error set_null when a column list is given. It sizes cstate->domain_with_constraint by the table's attribute count and indexes it by attribute number, so the NOT NULL domain check applies to the right column.

precedents_retrieved.title: Handling of the input data errors in COPY FROM
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add an IGNORE_ERRORS option to COPY FROM that skips malformed input rows with a WARNING instead of aborting the load. Rows with too few or extra columns are skipped directly, and type input errors are caught with PG_TRY/PG_CATCH around InputFunctionCall, without subtransactions.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier returned the entry because the last patch was five months old, no longer applied, and failed "git diff master --check". On the rebased patch, Alvaro Herrera objected that catching errors in a PG_TRY block and only logging a WARNING is unsafe. Out-of-memory, WAL write failures and serialization failures from triggers can leave memory or session state broken until the transaction aborts. Earlier, Peter Geoghegan said a design that uses subtransactions in a way not obvious to the user would be hard to sell to a committer.
matched_queries: COPY FROM STDIN error before input
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
After
looking at the way you're handling errors, it seems that you've chosen
to go precisely the way people were saying that was not admissible: use
a PG_TRY block, and when things go south, simply log a WARNING and move
on.  This is unsafe.

precedents_retrieved.title: Handling of the input data errors in COPY FROM
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Stephen Frost, Craig Ringer, Peter Eisentraut
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets COPY FROM skip input rows that have type or column errors instead of stopping at the first error. The posted version catches errors from input functions with PG_TRY() in NextCopyFrom and does not re-throw them.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Catching the error without PG_RE_THROW() skips the cleanup that AbortTransaction() does, such as resetting memory contexts, releasing locks and restoring user and security contexts. Input functions, including ones from extensions such as PostGIS, can do arbitrary work, so this is not safe. Reviewers suggested a subtransaction approach that retries a batch and skips the failed row. Peter Eisentraut returned the patch because it did not do this or a safe 'soft error' scheme, which Tom Lane also judged hard to make safe.
matched_queries: COPY FROM STDIN error before input
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: In the end, this isn't an acceptable approach to this problem.

precedents_retrieved.title: Improve handling of OOM errors in libpq making process hangling for COPY and bind (take 2)
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch fixes libpq hangs on out-of-memory errors while it parses COPY start and ParameterDescription messages. The parser leaves pqParseInput3 on error and keeps the first error message, so PQgetResult and PQexecFinish return the failure and do not wait for server input that will not come.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Heikki Linnakangas committed the ParameterDescription fix but did not commit the COPY part. He could not see why the PQexecFinish change was needed, and he found that if getCopyResult() fails with OOM, libpq stays in COPY_IN mode while PQexec() returns NULL, so the next PQexec() fails with "another command is already in progress". Michael Paquier later reported that Heikki could not convince himself the change was sane for the COPY protocol, and planned more testing with tools that use COPY through libpq.

precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Now, libpq is already in PGASYNC_COPY_IN mode, but PQexec() returned NULL because of the OOM, so the application doesn't know that it's in copy mode.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert my bad decision of about a year ago to make PortalDefineQuery responsible for copying the query string into the new Portal.
precedents_retrieved.summary: Revert my bad decision of about a year ago to make PortalDefineQuery responsible for copying the query string into the new Portal.  Such copying is unnecessary in the common code path through exec_simple_query, and in this case it can be enormously expensive because the string might contain a large number of individual commands; we were copying the entire, long string for each command, resulting in O(N^2) behavior for N commands. (This is the cause of bug #4079.)  A second problem with it is that PortalDefineQuery really can't risk error, because if it elog's before having set up the Portal, we will leak the plancache refcount that the caller is trying to hand off to the portal.  So go back to the design in which the caller is responsible for making sure everything is copied into the portal if necessary.

precedents_retrieved.title: Sequence Access Method
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a sequence access method (seqam) API, analogous to index access methods, so that a pluggable implementation selected with CREATE/ALTER SEQUENCE ... USING can control how sequence values are allocated and reset, aimed mainly at global sequences in clustering systems. Later versions keep a common sequence tuple with an opaque AM-specific 'amdata' column, add get/set state functions, DDL for creating sequence AMs, and a 'gapless' sequence example extension.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The reviewer did not accept the API design and asked for revisions that were still outstanding. In the final round, Heikki Linnakangas concluded that the single opaque amdata column should be replaced by AM-specific separate columns, noting that this would keep queries such as SELECT last_value FROM sequence working, and that the API's modelling after the indexam API also needed rework. The author said he had not had time to work on it in that commitfest and agreed to it being returned.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Several others have weighed in to support separate columns, too, so I think that is the consensus. Separate columns it is.

precedents_retrieved.title: Sequence Access Methods
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds sequence access methods, a pluggable layer, so that a sequence can use another allocation method through `CREATE SEQUENCE ... USING`, `ALTER SEQUENCE ... USING` or a `default_sequence_mgr` setting. Its main target is global sequences for clustering systems, and later versions add a contrib "gapless" sequence AM.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. Heikki Linnakangas questioned the level of abstraction in 2013 and 2014, but on 2016-04-05 Fabrízio de Royes Mello marked the patch Ready for Committer, one day before it was returned with feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: COPY WHERE clause generated/system column reference
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patches make COPY FROM ... WHERE work with generated columns: they expand virtual generated columns in the WHERE clause and compute stored generated columns before the WHERE clause is checked. They also reject system columns other than tableoid in the WHERE clause.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Peter Eisentraut committed a smaller fix that rejects generated columns in COPY FROM WHERE with a clear error, and left tableoid for a separate thread. He then argued that support should not be added, because generated columns belong to the target table while the WHERE clause filters input data. Masahiko Sawada had shown that computing stored generated columns before the WHERE clause runs them before BEFORE INSERT triggers, so the WHERE clause changes the row the trigger sees.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
This seems fundamentally wrong, because generated columns are a
property of the target table, but the COPY WHERE clause is meant to
filter the input data.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fallback table AM for relkinds without storage
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a fallback table AM whose callbacks all raise an error, and assign it to relkinds without storage (views, foreign tables, partitioned tables) so that rd_tableam is never NULL. A wrong call into the table AM API for such a relation would then raise an error instead of crashing the backend.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andres Freund objected that the patch moves relkind-specific logic, such as choosing the slot type, into an AM that should never be called. He suggested separate AMs instead, for example one for foreign tables and one for sequences. Michael Paquier agreed he was not comfortable passing relkind knowledge into the AM, and he returned the entry because he was not sure what the right design was.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
This doesn't seem like an advantage to me. Isn't this just pushing logic
away from a fairly obvious point into an AM that one would expect to
never actually get called?

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert error-throwing wrappers for the printf family of functions.
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert error-throwing wrappers for the printf family of functions.
Reverted commit(s): Add error-throwing wrappers for the printf family of functions.; Permit use of vsprintf() in PostgreSQL code.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit 16304a013432931e61e623c8d85e9fe24709d9ba, except
for its changes in src/port/snprintf.c; as well as commit
cac18a76bb6b08f1ecc2a85e46c9d2ab82dd9d23 which is no longer needed.

Fujii Masao reported that the previous commit caused failures in psql on
OS X, since if one exits the pager program early while viewing a query
result, psql sees an EPIPE error from fprintf --- and the wrapper function
thought that was reason to panic.  (It's a bit surprising that the same
does not happen on Linux.)  Further discussion among the security list
concluded that the risk of other such failures was far too great, and
that the one-size-fits-all approach to error handling embodied in the
previous patch is unlikely to be workable.

This leaves us again exposed to the possibility of the type of failure
envisioned in CVE-2015-3166.  However, that failure mode is strictly
hypothetical at this point: there is no concrete reason to believe that
an attacker could trigger information disclosure through the supposed
mechanism.  In the first place, the attack surface is fairly limited,
since so much of what the backend does with format strings goes through
stringinfo.c or psprintf(), and those already had adequate defenses.
In the second place, even granting that an unprivileged attacker could
control the occurrence of ENOMEM with some precision, it's a stretch to
believe that he could induce it just where the target buffer contains some
valuable information.  So we concluded that the risk of non-hypothetical
problems induced by the patch greatly outweighs the security risks.
We will therefore revert, and instead undertake closer analysis to
identify specific calls that may need hardening, rather than attempt a
universal solution.

We have kept the portion of the previous patch that improved snprintf.c's
handling of errors when it calls the platform's sprintf().  That seems to
be an unalloyed improvement.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found: the search returned no earlier attempt at moving the COPY FROM relkind check. The thread points to no earlier discussion of this idea; message #2 notes only that COPY TO and COPY FROM have long checked relkind at different stages, with no known reason for the difference.

Within the standards and compatibility angle I find no objection worth sending. The patch adds no syntax, keyword, GUC or catalog object, so nothing new needs pg_dump or psql support. The only user-visible change is which error a failing COPY FROM reports first. That command fails either way, and the new order matches COPY TO (message #8). psql already skips the in-line data when COPY FROM STDIN fails early, so scripts with in-line data end the same way. One point is outside this angle and should go to the API angle. file_fdw and other BeginCopyFrom() callers pass relations that are not valid COPY targets, such as foreign tables without insert support. Whether the moved check can affect those callers cannot be checked without the code.

v3 moves an existing relkind check inside copyfrom.c and creates no persistent or cross-node state: no on-disk, WAL, catalog or protocol change, and the BeginCopyFrom() signature is unchanged. Tablesync and file_fdw call BeginCopyFrom() with tables or foreign tables, which pass the check, and a reviewer reports that file_fdw passes. Without the code, I could not check out-of-tree extensions that call BeginCopyFrom() on other relation kinds.

The patch adds no privilege or exposure surface. Permission checks in DoCopy() still run before the moved relkind check, and the relkind it reports is already visible in pg_class. With the change, COPY FROM PROGRAM and COPY FROM a file on an unsupported target no longer run the program or open the file, which slightly reduces what the command does before it fails.

From the maintenance angle the change is small, touches one file, adds nothing to the per-row path, and copies the placement COPY TO already uses. The only open point is the effect on BeginCopyFrom() as an API used by extensions.

Postgres has no option, setting or extension that makes COPY FROM reject a sequence or view before it reads input. The patch moves an existing check to an earlier point and adds no new mechanism, so this angle has nothing to raise. Code-level effects on other BeginCopyFrom() callers could not be checked.

No demand objection applies. The change is a small error-placement fix in one file, and it touches no catalog, syntax or GUC. Its benefit reaches any user who runs COPY FROM on a sequence, view or matview, and it stops a COPY FROM PROGRAM that will fail from running its command (message #6). Four reviewers reproduced the problem and agreed (messages #2, #4-#6). The cost to non-users is close to nothing, so the accumulation test (item 5) does not fail.
